text:
Noah Brooks: Morning! first day and stuck on kube access. I ran the macOS setup but `kubectl config get-contexts` only shows 'default' and `kubectl` prompts for password when I try SSO. Need a dev ns (noah-dev). Who to ping?

Elena Morales: welcome Noah :wave: Are you using the `redwood-sso` wrapper or the raw Okta CLI? On macOS we recommend the wrapper because it manages the kubeconfig merge.

Noah Brooks: I used the Okta CLI directly because the README mentioned it. I ran `okta-aws login` then `kubectl config view --raw` shows user `noah@redwood.ai` (no okta: prefix). Also my laptop is M1.

Jared Kim: the M1 binary path sometimes conflicts if theres an older kubectl plugin. Can you run `which redwood-sso && redwood-sso --version` and `kubectl plugin list`?

Noah Brooks: outputs:
```
/usr/local/bin/redwood-sso
redwood-sso v0.9.2
kubectl plugin list: kubectl-ns
```

Noah Brooks: the plugin might be overriding exec behavior?

Jared Kim: possible. Also check `kubectl config view --minify --raw` contexts block and paste sanitized.

Noah Brooks: sanitized:
```
contexts:
- context:
    cluster: redwood-dev
    user: noah@redwood.ai
  name: redwood-dev
```

Elena Morales: yep looks like the exec plugin block wasn't written. Two routes: 1) re-run `redwood-sso login --okta --write-kubeconfig` which writes the exec plugin; or 2) we can do a directory sync and create the ns so you can start while you debug. Which do you prefer?

Noah Brooks: try the login flag first: `redwood-sso login --okta --write-kubeconfig` gave "okta-client: wrote exec plugin" then `kubectl auth can-i list pods -n noah-dev` -> "error: You must be logged in to the server"

Jared Kim: that error usually means the token wasn't persisted or Okta group mapping missing. @infra-bot can you check okta groups for noah@redwood.ai and trigger a sync if needed?

infra-bot: okta group membership check: user not in group k8s-dev-access. Queuing group add job (job id grp-add-2026-12-08-09).

infra-bot: group add completed and directory sync started (job id sync-2026-12-08-09).

Elena Morales: once sync finishes, we'll create namespace `noah-dev` and RoleBinding `rb-noah-dev-edit` binding `edit` to `okta:noah@redwood.ai`.

infra-bot: sync completed. Proceeding to apply namespace and RoleBinding.

infra-bot: namespace `noah-dev` created, RoleBinding `rb-noah-dev-edit` applied.

Noah Brooks: `kubectl get pods -n noah-dev` -> "no resources found". I can list now. Set default ns with `kubectl config set-context --current --namespace=noah-dev` and port-forward works. Thanks y'all! :tada:

Jared Kim: added a quick macOS note to the onboarding doc about plugin collision and `--write-kubeconfig`. Also note the Okta-group step; often the symptom is the user shown without the `okta:` prefix.

Noah Brooks: awesome, really appreciate the quick help. One follow-up: later I'll need a CI service account for running preview jobs. Where to request?

Elena Morales: open a ticket in #eng-infra with SA name and required verbs. We prefer namespaced SAs for dev work.

Noah Brooks: will do. Thanks everyone!
